sources.entry: TimeTagger - An open source time-tracker based on an interactive timeline and powerful reporting. (Demo, Source Code) GPL-3.0 Python

summary.one_liner: TimeTagger is an open source, web-based time tracker that runs locally or on a server, built around an interactive timeline and tag-based reporting.
summary.what_it_does: It provides a timeline-based UI for recording time and uses tags rather than projects to organize entries. It generates reports in PDF and CSV and lets users set daily, weekly, or monthly targets. It includes an experimental integrated Pomodoro timer and a responsive layout for small and large screens. Data syncs between devices, and the server can run in single-user mode on localhost or with multiple users via credentials or a reverse proxy header. Data is stored in SQLite via itemdb.
use_cases: generate PDF or CSV time reports
set daily or weekly work targets
how_to_run: Optional: docker-compose using the images from the GitHub container registry (docker-compose.yml or docker-compose.nonroot.yml)
Optional: python -m timetagger --credentials=user:bcrypt_hash for multi-user login
Optional: enable reverse proxy auth with --proxy_auth_enabled=True --proxy_auth_trusted=IP --proxy_auth_header=X-Remote-User
Developers: git clone the repo, then pip install -e .
notable: Interactive timeline as the main interface instead of project lists
Client written in Python and compiled to JavaScript with PScript
Can run single-user out of the box on a local machine
Supports reverse-proxy authentication (e.g. Authelia) via HTTP header
Developer tooling uses invoke, black, flake8, and pytest
caveats: Multi-user access requires configuring credentials or a reverse proxy
A hosted version is available as a paid account (about €3 per month), which the README mentions as an alternative to self-hosting
